h: Getting round the course in style
p: This is an 18+ venue from top to bottom, so it's all about grown-up fun. A round of crazy golf is one of those rare activities where talent counts for very little, so don't be put off if your group has a mix of sporty and not-so-sporty types. A light touch beats a big swing almost every time, and the trickiest holes reward patience more than power.

For the best night, book a slot that suits your plans. An early-evening round works well before dinner, while a later tee time can kick off a proper night out. Settle teams, forfeits and side bets before you start, keep things moving for the groups behind you, and have one fair-minded scorekeeper rather than everyone keeping their own (wildly different) totals.

Liverpool is a cracking city for a weekend. The Royal Albert Dock has the Merseyside Maritime Museum, the International Slavery Museum and The Beatles Story, and it's lovely for a waterside wander. The Pier Head with the Royal Liver Building is a short walk away, and the Mersey Ferry gives you great views of the skyline. For nights out, Bold Street, the Baltic Triangle and the Ropewalks area are packed with bars and restaurants, and Mathew Street, home of the Cavern Club, is the place for music fans. Merseyrail makes it easy to get in and out of the city centre without a car.
